claims.statement: internal/subscription's package doc states the entire multi-profile design rests on one confirmed fact: every supported vendor CLI selects its configuration directory from an environment variable, and many-ai-cli only ever creates a directory and sets that one variable, never reading, writing, parsing, or storing the credential itself.

A spawn with no subscription profile selected must produce a byte-for-byte identical environment to an unmodified spawn (enforced by TestSubscriptionLaunchWithoutProfileLeavesEnvUnchanged), and a live session's credentials are never swapped mid-session, enforced by TestLiveSessionAuthIsNeverSwapped scanning the source for such an assignment rather than relying only on a runtime test.

internal/subscription's package doc states remaining usage quota cannot be queried from any vendor CLI (measured 2026-08-17), so there is deliberately no ReadUsage method on the provider Adapter interface; this is stated as distinct from whether usage data exists at all, since three separate local-file data paths do exist and are read by the Hub.

seed.go's package doc states three rules bound what a fresh subscription profile inherits: entries are carried in only additively (never overwriting, renaming, merging, or deleting something already present in the profile), every seed write lands only under ~/.many-ai-cli/subscriptions/ so the user's real ~/.claude/~/.codex/~/.grok are read but never written, and each provider adapter lists exactly which entries to carry by name rather than copying an entire directory wholesale.

SeedCopyFile copies a file as-is and is used for files the vendor CLI itself rewrites (settings.json, config.toml), because a symlink there would push the profile's own edits back into the user's default configuration; SeedLinkDir instead links a whole directory (symlink, or a junction on Windows) for content the user maintains in one place, such as skills, slash commands, and prompts, so a later addition reaches every profile without a re-seed.

usagerelay's package doc states a hard security requirement: only numeric metadata (token counts, cost, model name, elapsed time) from Claude's statusLine hook or Codex's Stop hook is ever sent to the Hub's /api/session-usage endpoint; for Codex's rollout JSONL specifically, only the numeric fields of token_count events are extracted and conversation-body lines are read and discarded without ever being held in memory, and an HTTP send failure logs a stderr warning but still exits 0 so the vendor CLI's own hook is never broken.
